transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess... I’m just tired all the time. Not just regular end-of-the-school-day tired. Even if I sleep a full night, I still have to really push myself to get through grading, making dinner, getting ready for the next morning. It’s been wearing on me.
Have you been feeling down or hopeless most of the day, more days than not, even when things go okay?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can still smile at school and do what I need to do, but most days there’s this kind of gray, flat feeling underneath. It follows me home, and even things I usually like, like my garden or painting, feel… distant.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things you used to, like your garden or painting, as much as you did before?
I’m not sure. I mean… I still do them sometimes. It just doesn’t feel quite the same, I guess.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or depressed most of the day, even after you've had a good night's sleep?

Yeah… most days, I think. I can get through school and smile for the kids, but underneath it’s just kind of gray and flat. Even after sleeping, it sort of follows me home. My garden or watercolors feel… far away.
Do you feel fatigued or like you have no energy most days, even after a good night's sleep?

Yeah… that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I’m tired all the time. Not just normal after-school tired, but… even if I sleep, I still have to kind of force myself through grading, making dinner, getting ready for the next day.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, don’t give you the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction anymore?
I don’t really know. Maybe a little, but I still do them sometimes. It’s hard to say if it’s… less pleasure, exactly.
Do you find that you feel down or depressed most days, even when things in your life are going well?

Yeah… I think so. Even when nothing is really wrong, like work is okay or the day goes fine, there’s still this flat, gray feeling underneath. I can act normal with my students, but it kind of comes home with me.
Have you noticed that you no longer feel pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting?
I’m not sure. I mean, I still do those things sometimes. I wouldn’t say there’s no interest… it’s just hard to tell.
Would you say that you feel down or depressed most days, even when things in your life are going fine, like at work or at home?
Yeah… most days, I think. I can still smile and get through things at school, but underneath it’s just kind of gray. Even when home or work is fine, it follows me.
Would you say that you feel down or depressed most days, even when things in your life are going fine, like at work or at home?

Yeah… I know I’ve said it, but yes. Most days I can get through school and smile for the kids, but underneath it’s just this flat, gray feeling. It kind of comes home with me, and even things like the garden or painting feel… far away.
Do you feel down or depressed even on days when nothing particularly stressful or upsetting has happened?
Yeah… even when nothing really happened. I can still smile for my students and get through the day, but underneath it’s just sort of gray and flat. It follows me home, I guess.
Would you say that your mood is depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even when nothing particularly bad has happened?
Yes… most days. I can still teach and smile when I need to, but underneath it’s this kind of gray, flat feeling. It follows me home, even when nothing bad happened.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?
I don’t know… not in any big way. I mean, I can still do what I need to do. Maybe I’m a little slower sometimes, but I haven’t really been tracking it.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do you still try them just out of habit even if they don’t feel the same?
I’m not really sure I’d say completely lost interest. I still do some things… maybe more because they’re there, or because I feel like I should. It just doesn’t always feel like much.
Would you say that you take no pleasure or interest at all in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do they still feel somewhat rewarding, even if not as much as before?
I’m… not sure. I wouldn’t say there’s no interest at all. Sometimes it feels okay for a little while, just not like it used to.
Would you say that you get absolutely no pleasure or interest from things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do they still feel at least a little rewarding sometimes?
I guess… maybe a little sometimes. I wouldn’t say absolutely no pleasure, but it’s not something I really think about much.
Would you say that you have completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do they still feel at least a little interesting or pleasurable sometimes?
I don’t think it’s completely gone. It’s just… muted, I guess. Sometimes there’s a little something there, but I don’t really know how to describe it.
Would you say that you have completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do they still feel somewhat meaningful or enjoyable at times?
I mean… not completely, I don’t think. There are times it feels a little worthwhile, but it’s pretty faint. I’m not sure how else to put it.
Would you say that you get absolutely no pleasure or interest from things you used to enjoy, like your garden or painting, or do they still feel at least a little rewarding sometimes?
I… I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say it’s absolutely nothing, but I also don’t feel much from it most of the time. Maybe a little, here and there.
